description: Agent-written SAS: what run_sas tells the model a submission produced, and how it decides a SAS session is safe to run agent code in. The tool's description is prompts/run-sas-tool.md, which both packages ship, so it is not repeated here. The source is tests/shared/run-sas.json; the copy under pkg-r/tests/testthat/fixtures/shared/ is generated by scripts/sync-shared.sh. Edit the source and re-run that script.

value.description: The model-facing value of one submission, from its log and its listing. A log message starts at a line beginning ERROR, WARNING, or NOTE (optionally followed by a message number such as `22-322`) and a colon, and runs on through the indented lines after it. Lines that are not part of a message, such as the echoed source, are dropped, as are NOTE messages reporting process time. Each line is right-trimmed. Form feeds are removed from the listing, each of its lines is right-trimmed, and leading blank lines and trailing whitespace are removed, so its columns stay aligned. The value joins, with a blank line between: an error notice when any message is an ERROR, `Output:` and the listing when it is not empty, and `Log:` and the messages when there are any. Each of the last two is cut at its limit, counting characters, followed by a line saying it was truncated. With neither listing nor messages, the value says the code produced no output. In a case, `$repeat:<c>:<n>` stands for the character c repeated n times, so a case can exceed a limit without carrying 10 kB of text.

probe.description: Before running agent code in a session, commons submits `code` and reads the session's XCMD setting from the log: the last line that is exactly `COMMONS_XCMD=` followed by a word, uppercased. The echoed source line does not count. Agent code runs only when the setting is NOXCMD; any other setting, or none found, refuses it, because a session that allows host commands lets agent code reach the server's shell.
